item.title: Should Red Sox Target Freddy Peralta In Free Agency?
item.description: Free agent pitcher Freddy Peralta The Boston Red Sox have a very good lineup and rotation when healthy, but injuries held them back last season. Even if they are healthy going into next season, they have some moves they need to make in the offseason. Sonny Gray was a huge part of the team last season, but he is a free agent now. The Red Sox could look to replace him on the open market. Obviously, Tarik Skubal is the top pitcher available, and the Red Sox are not really expected to go after him. However, they could consider going after Freddy Peralta, who is at worst the third best pitcher on the open market. Peralta was acquired by the New York Mets before the regular season, but traded to the Tampa Bay Rays at the deadline. Peralta was not good on the Mets, and the two-time All-Star looked like he was going to have to sign a prove it deal as a free agent. However, the Rays got him back to looking like an All-Star. Looking for the perfect gift for a baseball player in your life? Check out our brand new baseball lifestyle brand! The Rays had him throw his changeup more, pitch out the stretch and move his position on the rubber. All of that resulted in a 3.25 ERA for the Rays in 10 regular season starts. He had a 0.79 ERA in his final six regular season starts. Peralta was exceptional in the postseason and won the American League Championship Series MVP Award. He could join the Red Sox and round out a great starting rotation. Garrett Crochet, Payton Tolle, Ranger Suarez, Peralta and Jake Bennett would be a great group. item.title: Spain coach De la Fuente among mourners at tragic footballer De Miguel's funeral
item.description: Tenerife footballer Jesus de Miguel's funeral was attended by around 400 mourners (Cesar MANSO) Spain's World Cup-winning coach Luis de la Fuente and the president of Real Madrid were among several hundred mourners who paid their respects at Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel's funeral on Thursday. De Miguel, 30, died following a sickening collision with Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono during a second division match on Monday. Around 400 mourners, most dressed in traditional black, gathered outside the church in the village of Navahermosa, around 100 kilometres (62 miles) southwest of Madrid, to greet the funeral cortege. They included De la Fuente and Real Madrid chief Florentino Perez. Flags flew at half mast in Navahermosa, the birthplace of De Miguel's parents and where his grandparents still reside, after the council declared three days of mourning. "We do not have enough words to thank all those who have sent messages, called or attested how much affection they had for him," said De Miguel's agent, reading out a statement on behalf of the family, who stood with him outside the funeral home before setting off for the church. They added they would like their privacy to be respected and expressed "their need to be allowed to grieve in peace as is normal in such a situation." Once the cortege arrived at the church, De Miguel's Tenerife teammates acted as pall bearers and carried his coffin into the church. - 'Immense pain' - Earlier on Thursday Spain's footballers' union asked that all this weekend's matches be postponed as a mark of respect. The men and women players "in every category", who were polled by the AFE union, believe "unanimously" that this weekend's matches "should not be played", it said. Tenerife's second division match at Granada and Andorra's clash with Mallorca have already been postponed, as were several midweek cup fixtures. "The footballers have expressed their deep sorrow for this loss and do not believe that there are the psychological and humane conditions necessary for the competition to be played in normal circumstances," AFE added. Tenerife are to pay homage to De Miguel -- who last season played a pivotal role in the club being promoted to the second tier -- on Saturday afternoon at the club's stadium. Spanish police sources have told AFP an investigation into what happened has been opened, under judicial supervision. Owono, for his part, has been subjected to a torrent of online abuse, a lot of it racist. item.description: Ja Morant ditches signature locs and debuts new look after drastic haircut originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Out with the old, in with the new. Ja Morant is serving up a new look amid his injury recovery, where he is ditching his signature locs. In a video shared on Nov. 4, the Portland Trail Blazers star shocked the internet when he revealed that he will now be rocking a low cut instead of the locs fans have associated with his look. Big chop!!👀✂️ https://t.co/mfP85UJZVz — Catch12 (@Catch12media) November 5, 2026 Morant also shared a sequence of photos on his Instagram Wednesday that showed the hair stylist cutting off the locs. After a couple of slides showed his hair on the floor as he sat in the chair, a photo revealed Morant's reaction: a big smile as he gazed at half of his hair waiting to be cut, and then the other side showing his newly cut hair. Towards the end of the post, the last three photos showed Morant rocking the new cut underneath a green hat as he made his way onto a private plane. He most likely was boarding the plane to go to Arizona, where they faced the Phoenix Suns on Wednesday. Fans responded to the new cut in the comments, with one fan asking, "Freshman year cut ain’t it?" " he’s backkkkkkkkk," another fan wrote, adding the celebration emoji. The Trail Blazers defeated the Suns 132-119. While the Trail Blazers were able to pull off the win, Morant was sidelined due to a Grade 2 left hamstring strain he suffered last month. Morant reacted to how the injury and the mental toll it put on him. "You want to be out there knowing you can't. That's, I feel like, the even tougher part," Morant stated . "I feel like nobody in this league would get injured and, you know, be able to play and not play, pretty much, unless it's like something where we like, 'All right, if I go play, I maybe can hurt it worse or anything.'" "So mentally, it can have you down on yourself. Actually, it can make you, you know, question everything, like, 'Why it had to be me? Why at this time?'" While Morant is not on the court for now, the Trail Blazers will be back on the road again to face the Los Angeles Lakers on Nov. 6 at 10 p.m. ET. item.title: Spurs praise Fox for 'A-plus' defense with game on the line in win over Mavs
item.description: San Antonio Spurs guard De'Aaron Fox (4) goes to the basket against Dallas Mavericks' Cooper Flagg (32) and Daniel Gafford (21) during the first half of an NBA basketball game, Wednesday, Nov. 4, 2026, in San Antonio. (Darren Abate/AP Photo/Darren Abate) Victor Wembanyama had a career night with 52 points and 24 rebounds, but the Spurs needed some strong defense by De'Aaron Fox in the final seconds to pull out a 112-111 victory over the Dallas Mavericks on Wednesday night. Fox knew he had his work cut out for him when he found himself nose to nose with Kyrie Irving at the top of the key with 10 seconds left and the Spurs leading by a point before a sellout crowd of 18,354 at the Frost Bank Center. "He's one of the toughest covers ever," Fox said of the nine-time All-Star and holder of the venue's single-game scoring record. Fortunately for the Spurs, Fox was more than up to the difficult task against one of the NBA's all-time clutch performers. Irving started his dribble with about 7 seconds left, but Fox shadowed him at every turn and contested the shot strongly at the end, forcing Irving to miss badly on a 15-foot turnaround jumper with 2.5 seconds left. Dylan Harper then beat Naji Marshall for the rebound as the Spurs held on to improve to 6-2 with their sixth win in a row and second of the season against the Mavericks (4-4). Fox, who finished with 10 points and four assists, said he thought back to the days when "you play on-one-on and there's no help" as he faced off with Irving, who finished with a team-high 29 points on an inefficient 9-of-27 shooting from the field. "Just trying to press up, try to make him uncomfortable, which is a hard thing to do," Fox said. "You just try to force a tough shot because you know he's going to be able to create a shot. You just want to make it a shot he wants less than whatever he's thinking at the time. Then contest it." Irving, who scored 57 points for Cleveland against the Spurs at the Frost in March 2015, admitted Fox bothered him just enough. "I felt I got a good look and had my legs underneath me as well," Irving said. "D Fox did a great job of bumping me off my spot." Fox also received praise from his coach and teammates. "There may not be a scarier guy with the basketball in his hands in that moment," Spurs coach Mitch Johnson said. "That feels unguardable and he's going to get a very high-quality shot up. So for De'Aaron to be on an island then guard a few moves off the dribble and then stay down on a shot fake and then contest without fouling, yeah, it's an A-plus effort." Wembanyama agreed. "He was great," the French superstar said. "He did everything he was supposed to do. I'm really glad Dylan got that last rebound. That was a great possession from start to finish." item.title: Red Wings would be 'in a lot of trouble' without their goaltending depth
item.description: While John Gibson recovers from an upper-body injury, Michal Postava stands to gain ground with the Detroit Red Wings. Postava was on the ice long after the morning skate ended on Thursday, Nov. 5, honing his skills with the help of goaltending coach Michael Leighton. Postava was slated to back up Daniil Tarasov in the evening's game against the Vegas Golden Knights. Postava was called up Wednesday, the day after Gibson was injured late in the first period of Tuesday's 4-2 loss at the Tampa Bay Lightning . Coach Todd McLellan said Gibson was still being evaluated Thursday and is day-to-day. Having Postava in the system is like having an ace up one's sleeve. "Michal in particular, ever since he's come to North America, has done a real good job of working his way up in the Grand Rapids situation to taking over there and now working his way up to here," McLellan said after the morning skate. "His effort in Edmonton was very good. It was inspiring for the players, and when a young goalie can come up and do that, it's a real positive thing." This is Postava's second stint with the Wings, having been called up under emergency conditions during their trip out west after Tarasov suffered an injury during a practice on Oct. 21. Postava flew from Grand Rapids to Vancouver the morning of Oct. 22 and ended up relieving Gibson for the third period against the Canucks after the veteran was unable to play when he got something in his eye. Two nights later, Postava earned his first career NHL victory in his first start, at the Edmonton Oilers , stopping 24 shots in regulation and overtime before turning away all three shootout attempts he faced. He was sent back to the minors when the Wings returned to Detroit. Now he's back, and even just practicing with the Wings is a boost. RISING UP: J.T. Compher, Michael Rasmussen playing up to Red Wings' standard at last "First time was quick, and I am just happy to be there every day," Postava said. "Being here, it helps me to save these shots. It's hard shots and some clever shots. So it's been good working on it, and it helped me." Postava is a great story: A free agent signee in the summer of 2025, he received a two-year contract. He was earmarked to back up Sebastian Cossa, the franchise's pick at No. 15 in 2021. Cossa did play the majority of the games during the 2025-26 regular season – 39, to 25 by Postava – but when Cossa struggled down the stretch, Postava was handed the net and excelled, and he hasn't stopped. He was just selected as the AHL Goaltender of the Month for October after going 4-0 last month with a 1.25 goals-against average and a .954 save percentage. He joins Detroit with a perfect 5-0-0 record with a 1.20 goals-against average and a 0.955 save percentage in five starts with the Griffins during the 2026-27 season. To have three goaltenders they trust is a big comfort for the Wings. "I can't speak for every team, but the ones that I've been on, you plan for three NHL-caliber people," McLellan said.

item.title: Northamptonshire Steelbacks cricketer serves one-month ban for cocaine
item.description: Northamptonshire Steelbacks batter Chris Lynn was handed, and served, a one month ban following a positive drug test for cocaine after the club won the T20 Vitality Blast final on July 18th. The Cricket Regulator confirmed that Lynn produced an Adverse Analytical Finding (AAF) following a drug test taken on Finals Day and an investigation was launched. Lynn’s urine sample was sent to the WADA-accredited Laboratory in the Laboratoire Anti-Dopage, France for analysis and returned Adverse Analytical Findings (“AAF”) for cocaine’s Metabolite benzoylecgonine meaning that it was a violation of cricket’s anti-doping rule. Cocaine is a substance banned “In Competition” but the investigation found that Lynn had taken the drug on the night of July 15th into the early hours of July 16th outside of competition. Having also provided evidence supporting this position the regulator accepted that Lynn’s use of cocaine amounted to an out-of-competition ADR violation and was unrelated to sporting performance. The regulator charged Lynn with two ADR violations in September and sought a suspension of three months. The second of those violations – ADR Article 2.2 – in that the Cricketer Used a Prohibited Substance, namely cocaine, on or before 18 July 2026 (the “ADRVs”) – was withdrawn as the reported level of cocaine in the sample was below the minimum reporting level required. Lynn acknowledged and accepted the findings of the regulator and informed them of his decision to undergo a substance of abuse treatment programme. In October, the regulator received evidence that Lynn had completed the programme and his suspension was reduced to one month. That ban was served between Lynn’s provisional suspension on 31 July 2026 until 11.59pm on 30 August 2026. Northants beat Hampshire in the Vitality Blast T20 final at Edgbaston this year (PA) The findings also concluded that there was no requirement to inflict any sanction Northamptonshire Steelbacks. A statement from the Cricket Regulator reads: “The Cricket Regulator has imposed a one-month suspension on former Northamptonshire Steelbacks cricketer Chris Lynn. The period of suspension has now been served. “Mr Lynn produced an Adverse Analytical Finding (AAF) for the presence of cocaine's Metabolite, benzoylecgonine, related to an In Competition sample collected on the 18 July 2026. “Mr Lynn has accepted the sanction. No further comment will be made on this matter.”

item.title: Diana Taurasi headlines 2027 Women’s Basketball Hall of Fame class
item.description: Two elite scorers, a pair of championship-winning WNBA coaches, a longtime referee and a trailblazing administrator will make up the next class inducted into the Women’s Basketball Hall of Fame. The Hall of Fame – based in Knoxville, Tennessee – announced the 2027 class on Thursday, Nov. 5. It includes WNBA all-time leading scorer Diana Taurasi , the legendary Iowa sharpshooter "Machine Gun" Molly Bolin Kazmer, WNBA coaches Sandy Brondello and Mike Thibault, refereeing veteran Dee Kantner and Dr. Judith Holland, the former director of women’s athletics at UCLA. The induction ceremony for these six inductees will be held Saturday, June 26, 2027 in Knoxville. "For nearly thirty years, the Women’s Basketball Hall of Fame has honored the greatest of the game, and we are thrilled to welcome these six inductees into the distinguished seats of the Hall of Fame," Michelle Marciniak, CEO of the WBHOF said in a statement. item.description: BC Game was announced as a sponsor of Leicester City before the 2024-2025 season [Stephen White - CameraSport via Getty Images] A football fan group has expressed "dismay" that Leicester City's main shirt sponsor has appointed a porn actress as an ambassador. BC Game - which was named as a sponsor for the League One side at the start of the 2024-25 season - named Eva Elfie as a brand ambassador on Tuesday. The online gambling company posted a video of Elfie and a delivery driver on social media, with the caption: "Welcome to BC Game Eva Elfie! Let the fun begin." The Foxes Trust said gambling and pornography could have "devastating impacts", and added: "Partnerships like these bring these two worlds to a larger audience and, by association, link them to Leicester City." In a statement entitled "BC Game - It gets worse", the trust said: "Most Leicester City supporters will know by now the trust's dismay and discontent with BC Game being our front of shirt sponsor. "BC Game have now announced a new partnership with 'international content creator and esports personality' Eva Elfie... who just happens to be an international porn star. "From the moment the club decided to take sponsorship from a betting company we felt Leicester City were ditching its values. "Now throw into the mix that BC Game have entered into a partnership with someone who continues to make their name via adult content. "Both gambling and pornography can have devastating impacts on people's lives, in particular young people. "Partnerships like these bring these two worlds to a larger audience and, by association, link them to Leicester City. Is this who we are now?" In a post on LinkedIn on Tuesday, BC Game said Elfie had an "established presence in gaming communities". Chief executive Ali "Ako" Muhanned said: "Eva has built an incredible relationship with the gaming and esports community through genuine passion and consistent content creation." Announcing the club's partnership in 2024, Leicester City said BC Game - which is not available to users in the UK - was a "socially responsible platform" and aimed to provide an "enjoyable and safe gaming experience". Susan Whelan, the former club chief executive, previously said: "We welcome BC Game to Leicester City - an opportunity to work with an innovative partner in a new category for the club.
